submission.justification: Through systematic simulation and optimization, Absorber-F3 at 4.6 mm plate thickness achieves the best energy resolution of 3.077% at 100 GeV. The optimization process involved: (1) Initial screening of all three candidates at 5 mm showing F3 superior at 3.2%, compared to F1 at 3.9% and F2 at 5.1%; (2) Coarse scan of F3 across the full 2-10 mm range identifying the 4-6 mm region as optimal; (3) Fine-grained refinement testing thicknesses from 4.25-5.5 mm in small increments, confirming 4.6 mm as optimal with 3.077% resolution. This represents a 4% improvement over the initial 5 mm baseline. F3's shortest radiation length enables superior shower sampling and energy measurement. The material has been verified to allow hands-on maintenance during shutdowns, meeting all operational constraints.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F3 at 4.6 mm achieves 3.077% energy resolution, which is the best result found across all materials and thicknesses tested. This outperforms F1 (3.9% at 5mm) and F2 (5.1% at 5mm), and represents the optimum from refined scanning.

requirements.requirement: The absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F3 is one of the three candidate materials evaluated (F1, F2, F3) from the specifications.

requirements.requirement: The calorimeter must allow hands-on maintenance during shutdowns
requirements.evidence: Hands-on maintenance has been verified as feasible (hands_on_maintenance_verified = 1), confirming F3 meets radiation safety requirements for direct access during shutdown periods.
The recommended plate thickness of 4.6 mm falls within the specified constraint range of 2-10 mm.
